target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (Fm S₀ S : Type) [LogicalConnective Fm] [LogicalNeutral Fm] [Entailment S₀ Fm] [Entailment S Fm]
    (𝓑 : S₀) (𝓢 : S) [Entailment.Cl 𝓑] [Entailment.Cl 𝓢] (K F : Fm → Fm),
    Def1 𝓑 𝓢 K → Def2 𝓢 K → Def3 𝓢 K →
    Def5 𝓑 F →
    (∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (F φ 🡒 φ)) →
    ∃ ψ, 𝓢 ⊢ K ψ ⋏ ∼F ψ
translation: Target is the proposition asserting that for all arbitrary types Fm (sentences), S₀, and S (proof systems), every choice of formal propositional connectives (implication 🡒, conjunction ⋏, disjunction ⋎, negation ∼) and constants (⊤, ⊥) on Fm, every choice of provability relations on Fm for systems of types S₀ and S, every system 𝓑 : S₀ and every system 𝓢 : S that each prove all classical propositional tautologies in these connectives and are closed under modus ponens, and every pair of functions K, F : Fm → Fm, if the following five hypotheses hold: (1) [Def1] for every sentence φ : Fm, if 𝓑 proves φ then 𝓢 proves K φ; (2) [Def2] for all sentences φ, ψ : Fm, 𝓢 proves K (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡒 (K φ 🡒 K ψ); (3) [Def3] for every sentence φ : Fm, 𝓢 proves (K φ) 🡒 φ; (4) [Def5] there exists a sentence ψ : Fm such that 𝓑 proves ψ 🡘 ∼(F ψ) (i.e., (ψ 🡒 ∼(F ψ)) ⋏ (∼(F ψ) 🡒 ψ)); and (5) for every sentence φ : Fm, 𝓢 proves K ((F φ) 🡒 φ); then there exists a sentence ψ : Fm such that 𝓢 proves (K ψ) ⋏ ∼(F ψ). The existential quantifier over ψ in the conclusion is scoped independently of the existential quantifier over ψ in hypothesis (4), so the statement does not explicitly require the two witnesses to be the same sentence. Nothing else is required: Def4 (that 𝓢 proves K ((K φ) 🡒 φ) for all φ) is not assumed; neither 𝓑 nor 𝓢 is required to be consistent; 𝓢 is not required to satisfy the rule from 𝓢 ⊢ φ to 𝓢 ⊢ K φ; no properties of F other than hypotheses (4) and (5) are assumed; and the types Fm, S₀, S and functions K, F carry no built-in arithmetic, Gödel numbering, or internal quantifiers.

divergences.description: In Theorem 3, the assumption that S includes EA and that F(x) is a formula with one free variable automatically yields the diagonal fixed point for ¬F(x) via arithmetic and Gödel numbering. In Target, because arithmetic and Gödel numbering are not modelled (as declared), the existence of the fixed point (Def5 𝓑 F) is supplied as an explicit hypothesis, and 'S includes EA' is generalized to the minimal classical/modal hypotheses Def1, Def2, and Def3 (a harmless abstraction/strengthening).

Relative to Gödel's second claim (EA_T ⊢ K(F ⊆ T) → F ⊊ K) and Penrose's claim in [P-K356], Target formalizes the meta-level schematic conditional of Theorem 3 ((∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ K (F φ 🡒 φ)) → ∃ ψ, 𝓢 ⊢ K ψ ⋏ ∼F ψ) rather than an object-language conditional involving a truth predicate T, object-language quantifiers for K(F ⊆ T) and ¬(K ⊆ F), or a formalization of 'formal system' / 'algorithm'. Bridging from Target to the object-language claim in EA_T requires modelling T and quantifiers (outside the declared abstract scope) and instantiating 𝓢 to EA_T + K(F ⊆ T).

judgement.summary: Within its declared abstract setting, Target faithfully formalizes the consequence of Reinhardt's Theorem 3 under factivity (Def3), preserving the exact conditional structure, modal operators, and separation between the base theory 𝓑 (EA) and extending system 𝓢. The only caveats are minor idealizations inherent to the abstract setting: assuming the diagonal fixed point explicitly (Def5) and expressing the meta-level schematic conditional of Theorem 3 rather than the object-language truth-theoretic conditional of Gödel's second claim.
